title: The compliance queue never sleeps. Neither did I.
summary: A former global intake and conflicts leader on why law firm growth is outpacing compliance, and how agents can take on prep so experts focus on judgment.
body_markdown:
I’ve been the person fielding calls from frustrated partners wondering why their matter wasn’t open.


I’ve been the leader staring at the conflicts queue late at night and first thing in the morning, reviewing the request list with my team and wondering: **How are we ever going to clear this backlog?**


I’ve been the point person for senior leadership when they needed to get their hands on meaningful reporting and insights, only to struggle to pull it together.


For several years, I ran global new business intake and conflicts at one of the world’s largest law firms. I watched the same challenge intensify year after year: more matters, more laterals, increasingly complex client portfolios, and more outside counsel guidelines arriving by email. The firm was growing, but the workload was growing even faster.


On the other side of all of this was a talented, dedicated team expected to move just as fast in opening matters for billing, without sacrificing the quality of the risk checks.


In a recent webinar, I stepped into several roles to demonstrate situations that law firm leaders and teams encounter every day. Together with our Product team, I showed[Intapp Compliance with Celeste](https://www.intapp.com/compliance/) in action and the value it can deliver for partners, compliance professionals, and firm leadership.


## Growth is outpacing what compliance was built to handle


Let’s start by thinking about the partner experience. Partners want to accept new work and build momentum quickly. Instead, they are often met with an administratively burdensome process that delays matter opening and affects the client experience.


During the webinar, I stepped into this scenario with a partner starting their day by scanning their inbox. The team needed to begin work urgently, however there was still no matter number, which meant they could not record their time. As the partner, I had lost track of where the request was in the process. Normally, I’d email my assistant or try to figure out who in the new business intake team to contact to help track it down. It was time-consuming and frustrating.


In the webinar, we highlighted how a partner can initiate a new matter request with one click, directly from their Outlook inbox. Celeste scans the email thread, checks whether the client already exists in the firm’s systems, and automatically creates the intake request, assigning it straight to the partner’s assistant for review and completion. Every field completed by the agent is highlighted on the form, including the client’s address, matter description, and related parties. The assistant can immediately see what Celeste has completed and what still requires review and completion by them before submission. As the partner, I clicked one button, and my assistant already had a request that was largely complete. The assistant’s job changed from creating a request and manually completing each field to reviewing, editing, and adding information as required.


### Clearing a stuck matter request without leaving the inbox


On the conflicts side, analysts can spend a significant part of their day on manual, administratively intensive tasks before they reach the analysis and judgment calls that require their expertise. These tasks include identifying aliases, building corporate trees, conducting sanctions and watchlist screening, and constructing search terms. I watched my team complete these steps repeatedly, with some complex searches taking hours. Conflicts expertise can take years to develop, yet highly skilled analysts still spend a substantial amount of time on the preliminary mechanics of the process.


Our Product team showcased a similar shift on the conflicts side. When a prospective client search came in for a retail portfolio acquisition, the playbook built the search strategy: validating names, building every alias automatically, pulling in the corporate family, running the search, and leaving a full summary of what Celeste did. It is not only relevant to preliminary conflicts checks. The same applies to conflicts checks that need to be run as part of the matter opening process, with a first version of the search already built and run before an analyst opens the request. It acts as a digital coworker alongside the conflicts analyst, completing the preparation before the analyst begins their review. Analysts get a head start and can focus their time on higher-value risk review, analysis, and judgment.


### Building a conflicts search before the analyst opens it


For firms riding the current wave of lateral hiring, this matters in a way managing partners and COOs feel directly. A playbook applies the same search strategy to every request, so a new analyst starts from the same standard as a seasoned one. Agents and playbooks can help firms handle more work without relying solely on additional headcount.


Compliance teams have been asked to absorb more volume, more complexity, and more lateral activity with processes that were never designed to scale in this way. This is not a failure of the compliance function. Until now, many firms have had few alternatives beyond hiring more people, moving resources between tasks, or postponing strategic projects simply to manage business-as-usual workloads. Technology is changing that equation, creating an important inflection point for firms.


We demonstrated what this shift looks like from an entirely different perspective: that of a firm COO or executive leader. As COO, the firm’s managing partner needed information quickly on how many conflicts and intake requests had been submitted during a six-month period, together with the time required to complete the conflicts and intake processes. Today, this task typically entails someone pulling reports from several systems and stitching them together in a spreadsheet. It is often a time-consuming exercise, with limited confidence in the result. We also demonstrated how Celeste is evolving to bring intake and conflicts data together on demand: search volume by analyst and search type, end-to-end time to open matters, where requests sit in the lifecycle, and the bottlenecks and trends. Getting that information on demand, instead of waiting for someone to assemble it, gives leaders a way to see workloads, bottlenecks, and roadblocks as they form.


### Pulling six months of intake and conflicts data on demand


## Risk doesn’t stop at matter opening


Risk management does not end when the matter opens. Months later, a client’s circumstances may have changed, a new party may have been introduced, or a new set of outside counsel guidelines may have arrived.


During the webinar, I stepped into a further scenario: it is Friday afternoon, the security team flags a suspected incident, client data may have been exposed, and the first call must go to general counsel. Before that call, however, I need answers. Which clients require notification, and what is the agreed timeline? The answer is usually buried across dozens of outside counsel guidelines, some requiring notice within twenty-four hours and others within seventy-two, and some naming a specific contract. Normally, answering those questions would require the team to manually review client terms and compile large volumes of information in spreadsheets, potentially working throughout the weekend. Even then, we might reach Monday with only a partial picture.


In the demo, we highlighted that no one needed to read every outside counsel guideline, and no one needed to work through the weekend. Celeste identified the relevant client-notification obligations, grouped them by response window, and linked each obligation to the underlying agreed language rather than providing only a summary. It also compiled the findings into the firm’s preferred report format, ready for the incident-response team. I went from “Where do I even start?” to “Here’s our plan” without anyone giving up the weekend.


### Turning a weekend of spreadsheets into a breach report


## What this actually changes


Firms moving forward with this technology are not doing so simply because they have read a report about AI. They are responding to practical business pressures: managing partners asking why lateral clearance is still so slow, growing volumes and complexity, and talented professionals spending too much time on repetitive tasks. The gap between what the compliance function can handle and what the firm needs continues to widen.


Compliance with Celeste does not replace the expert. It works alongside expert teams, completing labor-intensive preparation so that human judgment can be applied to more work.


That is what I wish I had: an agent that could take on repetitive manual preparation and give my team more time to focus on the decisions only they could make.
